test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 2 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: With reference to GPS, which of the following is correct?

options.text: Mountains and building blocks can act as obstacles to GPS signals.
Its full form is Global Placing System.
It has been developed by Russia
Its full form is Galileo Positioning System.

solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Mountains and building blocks can act as obstacles to GPS signals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GPS**

 
 
• The Global Positioning System, originally Navstar GPS, is a satellite-based radio navigation system owned by the United States government and operated by the United States Space Force.
 
• It is one of the global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) that provides geolocation and time information to a GPS receiver anywhere on or near the Earth where there is an unobstructed line of sight to four or more GPS satellites. Obstacles such as mountains and buildings block the relatively weak GPS signals.
 
• It is a satellite navigation system, used to determine the ground position of an object.
 
• It is based on a network of satellites orbiting above the Earth.
 
• It is based on the system of triangulation.
 
• It is a U.S.-owned utility that provides users with positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services.
 
• It is a network of 24 satellites that provides service to civilian and military users.
 
• **GPS** receivers provide location in terms of latitude, longitude, and altitude.
 
• The civilian service is freely available to all users on a continuous, worldwide basis.
 
• The military service is available to U.S. and allied armed forces as well as approved Government agencies.
 
• GPS is based on time and the known position of GPS-specialized satellites i.e **distance-based technology.** 
 
• GPS faces the problem of drifting due to continuous changes in the** position of satellites, and weak signals due to thick clouds and tall buildings. **
 
• GPS has a **voice system** to guide the user.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• China uses **BeiDou** as a Navigation System.
 
• India uses **NavIC** as a Navigation System
 
• **GLONASS, or "Global Navigation Satellite System"**, is used by Russia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Uses and Applications of** GPS**:

 
 
• There are five major uses of a GPS system. The applications that use GPS make use of any of these or a combination of all the five uses.
 
 
• Location - To determine positions.
 
• Navigation - To transfer from one place to another.
 
• Tracking - Monitoring movements of persons or objects.
 
• Mapping - Creating maps for generic as well as specific purposes.
 
• Timing - Accurately measuring time measurements.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Some of the major applications of GPS are as follows:**
 
 
• Emergency Systems - Fire alarms, smoke alarms, natural disaster early warning systems, etc.
 
• Entertainment - Games like Pokemon Go, PubG, and Free Fire use GPS to use locations.
 
• Household surveys - To create maps, plot charts and analyze area-specific, region specific or location specific population demographic trends.
 
• Micro-irrigation - To understand the needs of different variety of crops and their water needs.
 
• Air Traffic Controlling - Extremely important. Without ATC signal approval, no aircraft can take off or land on air stations.
 
• Marine Navigation System - Indian govt. recently designed the GEMINI system that makes the use of GAGAN, a GPS system for various purposes like - alerting fishermen about the marine accidents, probable fishing grounds, etc.
 
• Mining - For finding the exact geographical location for exploring and mining.
